newsitem.title: UK: Gold may see $400 before year-end - Merrill Lynch.
newsitem.headline: Gold may see $400 before year-end - Merrill Lynch.

text.p: Renewed interest by investment funds could push gold above the benchmark $400 per ounce level over the next few months, broker Merrill Lynch said.

An option play to squeeze prices higher is a likely scenario, but the rally would be short-lived, with a spike touching maximum levels of $415-20, analyst Ted Arnold said in the firm's latest Commodity Market Trends publication.
Gold fixed at $382.45 per ounce on Tuesday morning, the lowest level in two months.

"It is just that we are picking up enough vibes from U.S. funds expressing various levels of unease about bond and equity markets and the forthcoming U.S. presidential elections that we feel the gold market will advance more on technically-motivated buying than for any real fundamental reason," Arnold said.
Option volatilites are very low and could spur funds into using options to force prices higher.

"It would not surprise us if some big funds decided to run the market up through massive buying of out of the money calls and then aggressively buying the paper market and forcing the option grantors to frantically buy as well," Arnold said.
"But we strongly doubt if the higher prices will be sustained for any length of time," he added.
The longs would have to take profits and any faltering in the rally would provoke huge forward selling by gold miners, Arnold said.
South African gold houses would have good reason to lock in higher prices since the weaker rand is beginning to stabilise.
"Last but not least, we would expect to see some disinvestment selling coming out from the very price sensitive Middle East, Indian and Asian buying centres," the report said.
"So our advice to those readers of a naturally bullish nature is don't be bullish for too long," Arnold added.
